title: Workspace Heartbeat Executor Liveness v1
goal: Measure and operationally distinguish ChatGPT browser/UI disconnect from continued server-side assistant execution, then replace indefinite stale Heartbeat ownership with a bounded, fail-closed executor lease and safe takeover protocol so a fresh chat can recover without guessing or restarting the Heartbeat server.
acceptance_criteria: Document the exact signals available to a ChatGPT custom MCP server and explicitly distinguish them from unavailable internal ChatGPT turn-terminal events.
Record separate timestamps for model/executor activity and live-card/UI polling so browser disconnect can be observed independently from continued assistant-side activity.
Add a model-only executor lease/touch mechanism that does not create user-visible semantic heartbeat entries or pollute task history.
Expose a read-only liveness status that reports active owner, last model touch, last UI observation, lease expiry, and takeover eligibility without exposing the opaque openai/session identifier.
Keep current cross-conversation ownership fail-closed while a lease is fresh.
After a lease expires, allow an atomic explicit takeover that supersedes the stale turn and makes every later old-turn heartbeat/lease operation fail closed.

Require a fresh lease assertion before mutating external work after long waits or recovery boundaries; document that Heartbeat cannot physically block unrelated GitHub/tool mutations without a future orchestrator proxy.
Prove by tests that an expired writer can be replaced without a Heartbeat-server restart, an unexpired writer cannot be stolen, and a superseded old writer cannot renew or update its turn.

Prove in live ChatGPT use that the website/UI can stop or disconnect while executor touches continue, then that recovery becomes deterministically eligible only after the executor lease stops renewing.
Preserve all accepted v0.4.6 live-card sizing, turn-history, semantic heartbeat, and stale-turn isolation behavior.
constraints: Do not modify or deploy the live Heartbeat runtime until workspace-heartbeat-plugin-v1 v0.4.6 PR #155 completes its remaining host gates and is merged or otherwise durably accepted.
Do not claim exact internal ChatGPT executor death is observable unless OpenAI exposes a documented ChatGPT turn/session terminal signal to custom MCP servers.
Do not treat an individual Streamable HTTP request/socket close as assistant-turn death; the current server creates a request-scoped MCP transport.
Keep executor lease traffic separate from user-facing semantic heartbeat history and UI updates.
Use _meta["openai/session"] only as anonymized conversation ownership evidence; never expose or persist it in operator-visible output.
Do not weaken current cross-conversation ownership merely to recover faster; takeover requires an expired lease and must atomically fence the old turn.
Do not rely on a guessed 40-minute timeout. Current field evidence includes one Heartbeat turn with updates spanning about 47 minutes and another spanning about 37 minutes.
Do not claim the Heartbeat server can physically prevent direct mutations through unrelated tools; enforcement outside Heartbeat remains an executor/procedure contract unless a future proxy is added.
Persist design/acceptance evidence in workspace-control, but keep per-touch runtime lease state ephemeral.

inputs: Heartbeat task history from real long-running ChatGPT turns
user-observed website connection interruption while Heartbeat updates continue
outputs: executor lease data model and takeover state machine

evidence: Heartbeat turn 61947087-4246-41ae-a91c-5f52f5c64968 emitted from 2026-10-22T22:46:15.335Z through 2026-10-22T23:33:22.291Z, about 47 minutes 7 seconds.
Heartbeat turn 98f8cc2b-f3da-4821-ae02-33ac62039df3 emitted from 2026-10-22T23:51:47.088Z through 2026-10-23T00:28:39.472Z, about 36 minutes 52 seconds.
Observed duration is therefore variable and not consistent with a strict 40-minute hard stop.
HeartbeatStore retains ownerSessionId until terminal done or same-session supersession.
A different conversation is rejected while ownerSessionId remains set.
Current recovery after an unreachable owner is coordinated Heartbeat-server restart; there is no lease expiry.

validation.check: Current MCP transport cannot identify whole assistant-turn death
evidence: workspace-heartbeat server creates a new StreamableHTTPServerTransport and McpServer for each /mcp HTTP request and closes that transport on the individual response close event.
Therefore HTTP response close is request lifecycle, not the lifetime of the ChatGPT assistant executor.
Current ChatGPT tool metadata supplies anonymized openai/session conversation identity but no documented assistant-turn terminal event to this custom MCP server.

stages.resume_condition: v0.4.6 live-card release is accepted/merged and the liveness state machine is frozen before implementation.

outputs: tests and live observation evidence without automatic takeover
stages.resume_condition: Field evidence proves model and UI timestamps behave independently during a real frontend interruption.

outputs: bounded lease TTL selected from field evidence
old-turn fencing and pre-mutation lease assertion procedure
live handoff/recovery acceptance without server restart
stages.resume_condition: Observation data supports a TTL that avoids false takeover during normal long operations.

evidence: Workspace-control main before executor-liveness task creation.
Heartbeat v0.4.6 remains a separate open release PR #155 and must finish acceptance before liveness implementation is layered on top.

validation.check: User field evidence motivates new work
evidence: User observes ChatGPT website 'connection interrupted' before server-side execution stops; Heartbeat continues receiving updates after the website failure.
User also observes Heartbeat eventually stops, but current system gives no deterministic indication of when the executor has actually become unrecoverable.
Existing stale-owner recovery requires guessing or restarting the Heartbeat server.

blockers: Implementation/deployment is gated on completion or durable acceptance of workspace-heartbeat v0.4.6 PR #155 so this work does not invalidate its remaining live visual/handoff acceptance.
remaining_work: Finish the observability contract and exact state machine using current OpenAI documentation and live Heartbeat evidence.
After v0.4.6 acceptance, implement observation-only model-touch and UI-seen timestamps plus read-only liveness status.
Run a deliberate long-turn/frontend-interruption measurement and record the gap between UI last-seen and executor touches.
Choose a bounded lease TTL from measured behavior rather than a guessed chat duration.
Implement and validate atomic expired-owner takeover plus stale-writer fencing.
Update the canonical Heartbeat procedure with safe takeover/recovery rules and preserve restart as rollback.
next_safe_action: Do not change the live Heartbeat runtime yet. First finish/merge the pending v0.4.6 release PR #155 and its short-card, six-plus-update, and planned chat-handoff host gates. In parallel, freeze the executor-liveness state machine: separate last_model_touch_at from last_ui_seen_at; keep semantic heartbeats independent; define lease_expires_at and read-only status; permit takeover only after expiry; atomically supersede the old turn on takeover; make old-turn update/touch operations fail closed; and require a fresh lease assertion before post-wait mutating work. Then implement observation-only instrumentation on top of the accepted v0.4.6 source before enabling automatic takeover.
notes: Created from live field evidence on 2026-10-22/23. The user specifically observed the ChatGPT website disconnect while the server-side assistant continued to emit Heartbeat updates, followed later by Heartbeat silence. Current custom MCP tools do not receive a documented ChatGPT assistant-turn terminal event, so the design must distinguish exact internal death (currently unobservable) from operational liveness (measurable and recoverable). The proposed lease is intentionally machine-facing and must not reintroduce noisy timed semantic heartbeat updates.
